clue.text: Manage without a head in college

indicators.note: a head is a first letter, so the synonym for manage loses its opening letter

parts.note: to manage is to get on, as in coping or getting by

explanation.surface: Someone copes at college despite having no principal in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton is the famous English public school near Windsor, formally Eton College.

indicators.note: the letters of diner are put in a new order, as a dish is ordered from a menu

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A famous film star in a restaurant orders the duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' turns DINER into DENIR; the cricket duck, a zero score, adds O.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert De Niro is a celebrated American film star, so he is an example of an actor.

indicators.note: a pollarded tree has had its top cut off, so the tree's name loses its first letter

parts.note: the larch is a conifer

explanation.surface: A lopped tree stands in an entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch is a curved structure over an opening, the frame of a gate or entrance.

clue.text: Stroke with a bat, good cut

parts.note: to lance is to cut open, as a surgeon lances a boil

explanation.surface: A batsman plays a neat shot, nicely cut.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a glance is a deflecting stroke off the bat, usually down the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a glance is a light deflecting shot played with the bat, a kind of stroke.

parts.note: set means fixed or determined, as in set on going
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A firm decision is made about a squad's substitute player.
explanation.definitionFit: To set aside is to put away for later use, the verb sense of reserve.

clue.text: What a wizard might do, given a part in Pickwick papers?

definitions.meaning: a sorcerer's typical act is to utter an enchantment

definitions.text: given a part in Pickwick papers?
definitions.meaning: an actor chosen to play Solomon Pell, the attorney in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers, would be cast as him

explanation.surface: A magician's possible role in an adaptation of a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase as CAST AS PELL: Pell is a lawyer character in Dickens's Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard enchants people, while an actor picked for the role of Pell is cast in that part.

indicators.note: the letters of arrest me fly about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A demand to be arrested for flying a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' looks like it describes the flag, but it rearranges ARREST ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow banner or pennant, a kind of flag.

clue.text: Actress, with stitch in side, keeled over

indicators.note: in a down clue something keeled over is upturned, so the built word is read from the bottom
the word for stitch goes inside the word for side

parts.note: a side is a team
to stitch is to sew

explanation.surface: An actress with a painful stitch in her side collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' looks like part of the body with a stitch in it, but it means a team; 'in' builds the container and 'keeled over' turns the whole of it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Mae West was an American stage and screen star of the 1930s known for her wit.

indicators.note: the word for place holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: to lay is to place or put down

indicators.note: the word for tiny is read backwards

parts.note: wee is a Scottish word for small or tiny

explanation.surface: Somewhere with a tiny back room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back room' reads as one phrase, but 'back' turns the word for tiny round, 'containing' wraps it, and 'room' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is freedom of manoeuvre or margin, as in having room to move.

indicators.note: the kind of wood goes inside the word one

parts.note: fir is a softwood timber

explanation.surface: Timber burning inside a single stove.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alight and in flames is burning.

clue.text: Girls' night out in Perth — any drunk?

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering, so the letters of Perth and any are scrambled

explanation.surface: A women's celebration in the Scottish city of Perth: is anyone drunk?
explanation.definitionFit: A party for women only, held before a wedding, is a night out for the girls.

parts.note: a brilliant notion, read as a gifted rower at the stroke seat of the boat, the brilliant one at the stern

explanation.surface: A gifted rower comes up with a clever plan.
explanation.walkthrough: In rowing the stroke is the oarsman nearest the stern who sets the pace, so an exceptional one is a stroke of high talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden brilliant idea is described as a flash of inspired thought.

clue.text: Handy brute working in Canadian port

indicators.note: working signals the letters of handy brute being worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A useful thug employed in a harbour in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunder Bay is a city and harbour on Lake Superior in Ontario.

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Leaving the iron switched on is a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is someone who has committed a serious crime.

definitions.meaning: ... is a boiled or steamed suet pudding, as in plum ...
British slang for useless or worthless

explanation.definitionFit: Plum duff is a boiled dessert, and slang duff means worthless or faulty.

clue.text: Standard managed by team's leader is outrageous

parts.note: a standard is a flag
ran means managed, as in ran a business

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so take the opening letter of team's

explanation.surface: A flag organised by the team captain is shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means glaringly obvious and shocking, as outrageous behaviour is.

clue.text: Succeeded breaking into Russian city oil centre

indicators.note: the abbreviation for succeeded breaks into the city name

parts.note: Tula is a city south of Moscow
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone managed to break into a Russian city's oil installation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa in Oklahoma grew rich on petroleum and was called the Oil Capital of the World.

indicators.note: the word for try goes inside the race

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
to hear a case in court is to try it

explanation.surface: An attempt to compete in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' looks like an attempt, but it is a judge's sense, to try a case; the race is the Isle of Man motorcycle event.
explanation.definitionFit: At heart means fundamentally or in truth, as in deep down, which matches really.

indicators.note: something not finished lacks its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an event is a competition or contest

explanation.surface: A competition that is not over yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yet' looks like part of 'not finished yet', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and yet are both intensifiers before a comparative, as in even better or yet better.

clue.text: Name of deceased male found in a tube train?

definitions.meaning: a handle is slang for a name, so a dead man's name is his handle
a London Underground driver's cab has a safety control that stops the train if released

explanation.surface: Identifying a man who died on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: Handle is slang for a name; the tube is London's Underground railway, whose trains carry this safety lever.
explanation.definitionFit: The safety lever a driver must keep gripping, which halts the train if let go, has this grim name.

indicators.note: poorly suggests the letters of Graeme are in bad shape and rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Graeme is ill and painfully thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre describes a person who is lean and thin, like someone emaciated.

clue.text: Gold found under an overturned steamship in a bahamian port

indicators.note: in a down clue the symbol for gold sits below the other pieces
in a down clue the word an is turned upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Treasure discovered beneath a capsized steamer in a Caribbean harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' makes NA from AN; 'found under' puts AU at the bottom of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau is the capital and chief harbour of the Bahamas.

clue.text: Flying to barra, husband leaves a Scottish town

indicators.note: flying signals the letters of to barra being thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A husband departs from a Scottish town by plane for the island of Barra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' rearranges TO BARRA into ARBROAT; 'leaves' just links. Barra is a Hebridean island whose beach serves as its airstrip.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbroath is a fishing town on the Angus coast, famous for its smoked haddock.

clue.text: Expectation of the man without work

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for the man goes round the word for work

parts.note: he is the pronoun for the man
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: What an unemployed man looks forward to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but it is the old sense meaning outside, so the pronoun wraps round the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Hope is a wish that something will happen, an anticipation or expectancy.

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
someone sent away has been ordered to go

explanation.surface: A nod given when someone is told to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A nod of the head signals agreement or approval.

parts.note: North is one of the four players at bridge, abbreviated N
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A decent card player who needs a diamond suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice can mean proper or respectable, as in nice people.

indicators.note: the girl's name sits inside the abbreviation for British

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl draped in the Union Jack.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner is a cloth standard or flag carried on a pole.

clue.text: Sick patient injected with cocaine, a very small amount

indicators.note: the abbreviation for cocaine goes inside the rearranged letters
sick suggests the letters of patient are out of sorts and rearranged

parts.note: C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: An ill hospital patient is given a tiny dose of cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick' rearranges PATIENT into PITTANE, and 'injected with' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pittance is a meagre sum, especially of money.
